title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy, Tenure Track, Fall 2027
description:
Description

Chapman University invites applications for two tenure-track
positions at the rank of Assistant Professor in Philosophy,
beginning August 1, 2027. The appointments will be in the Smith
Institute for Political Economy and Philosophy and the Philosophy
Department within Schmid College of Science and Technology.

Successful candidates are expected to conduct independent and
original research at the highest academic level, provide excellent
teaching, and demonstrate academic leadership. Since the positions
are jointly appointed in the Smith Institute, we seek candidates
interested in working together with people from different
disciplinary backgrounds.

Chapman University is a nationally ranked, R2 Carnegie Classified,
private institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate
programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern
California’s most diverse and vibrant regions. Chapman’s campuses
are home to nearly 10,000 students representing 50 states, 4
territories, and 76 countries. The 11 schools and colleges of
Chapman, including Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and
Social Sciences, offer 50 bachelors, 29 masters, and 8 doctoral
programs, along with nearly 75 minors and 19 accelerated and bridge
programs. Classes are taught by the more than 1,100 dedicated
faculty members who are leaders in their fields, including Nobel
Prize recipients, MacArthur Fellows, National Medal of Science
honorees, former U.S. Supreme Court clerks, and Emmy, Grammy, and
Academy Award winners.

The mission of the Smith Institute is to reintegrate the study of
the humanities and economics in the spirit of Adam Smith, the
author of The Theory of Moral Sentiments and An
Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations,
and to recombine research and undergraduate education as a
discovery process in the spirit of Vernon Smith, a founder of
experimental economics.

Responsibilities:

Conduct independent and original research at the highest
academic level, publishing books and/or articles in peer-reviewed
journals, depending on the candidate’s specialty areas, and
extramural grant-seeking.
Teach undergraduate courses and mentor students in Chapman
University's Humanomics Program and Philosophy Department.
Initial teaching load is 2/2 for a total of 12 credit hours
annually.
Actively participate in Smith Institute and University service,
and community-engagement initiatives.
Tenure-track faculty are expected to develop and maintain an
active research agenda for future tenure consideration and are
evaluated on their research/scholarly activity, teaching and
service.

Qualifications

Of particular interest will be candidates specialized in one or
more of the following: Political Philosophy, Philosophy, Politics
and Economics, and the history of political and economic
thought.

Required:

PhD in Philosophy or its equivalent from an accredited
institution.
Strong potential for impactful scholarly contributions in the
field of Philosophy, or a closely related field.
Commitment to teaching and mentoring.

Preferred:

Prior teaching experience in undergraduate Philosophy (or
closely related field) and PPE courses.

Application Instructions

Application Instructions:

Interested and qualified candidates should submit:

Cover Letter
CV
Research Statement
Teaching Statement
Writing Sample
3 letters of Recommendation

For inquires please email: Samantha Aronson
saronson@chapman.edu

Successful completion of background check is required for final
candidate. The salary range for this position is $80,000 - $100,000
a year. Salary is competitive and will be commensurate with
experience. This position is contingent on final budget
approval.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Chapman University is an equal opportunity employer that provides
equal employment opportunities to all individuals, regardless of
their protected characteristics. All qualified applicants and

for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex,
sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national
